title: Huawei VRP: one case per device
mdr_note: Cases your own case rules open are Managed By Self, and Sophos MDR doesn't work them. The filter takes only the three Huawei VRP logging and local account changes custom detections, so Sophos's own detections still reach whoever works them today.
author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: An automatic case rule that opens one case per switch or router for the three Huawei VRP logging and local account changes rules, and adds that device's later detections to it while it's open. It brings its own case template, a Security Case with no assignee, and ships in Test state.
notes:
How it works:
- The filter takes only custom detections titled with one of the three rule names in rules/huawei/huawei-vrp-logging-and-local-account-changes. group_by takes the detection's host name, the switch or router, and adds this rule's name to it, so no other case rule can add to these cases.
- Case rules act only on Medium and higher detections. All of these rules are Medium or higher.
- A closed case isn't matched again: the next detection opens a new case.
- When it opens a case, it also adds earlier detections that fit its filter and group, even ones made before you added the rule. Sophos's Automatic cases page limits those to open detections of severity 0.6 and above (High and Critical), made within four hours of the detection that opened the case and not already in another case, up to 100. A lab tenant matched this: earlier Medium detections stayed out.

Setup:
- Import alone leaves the rule inactive: in a lab tenant an imported case rule opened no case until it was saved once more through updateCaseRule, with no change. The library's tools/case-rule-install.mjs imports the file and makes that call.
- Import puts the rule after your own case rules, whatever order the file has, so it moves none of them.

Testing:
- In a lab tenant on 2026-11-23, installed with tools/case-rule-install.mjs, it logged "case would have successfully been created but rule is in test mode" for a High Huawei VRP detection while in Test state.
- Enabled, it opened one case, Managed By Self, from a Medium password detection, and the case took the same switch's two earlier High detections. The other device's logging detection stayed out of it, and so did the switch's earlier Medium one.

Known gaps:
- Whether a Save in the console after Import does the same as updateCaseRule is unchecked.
